predecessors.note: "The states of Satara and Kolhapur came into being in 1707" over a succession dispute; the infobox has Kolhapur established in 1710 and the Tarabai page puts her rival court at Kolhapur in 1709.

successors.note: Acceded to the Dominion of India on 14 August 1947 and "merged into Bombay State" on 1 March 1949 (Kolhapur State page).

capitals.name: Kolhapur
capitals.note: Panhala is mentioned only as a hill fort, not as a capital.

rulers.name: Shivaji (I) of Kolhapur
rulers.note: Tarabai's son; deposed in 1714 by Rajasbai (Tarabai page); died 1726.

rulers.name: Sambhaji (III)
rulers.note: The Sambhaji II of Kolhapur page: "He ruled from 24 April 1813 to 2 July 1821" (infobox: Raja of Kolhapur, 24 Apr 1813 - 2 Jul 1821); the numbering differs between pages.

rulers.name: Shahu
rulers.note: The Shahu of Kolhapur page: "he was adopted by the Kolhapur royal family on 17 March 1884" and ascended the throne on 2 April 1894 (reign to 6 May 1922), with a regency council in between; the Kolhapur State page has Maharaja from 1900.

correction.text: the Kolhapur State: about 8,200 km2 including jagirs

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives no boundary and no area before 1901 (infobox 8,332 km2, text about 8,200 km2 including jagirs); a 50 km circle about Kolhapur (about 7,900 km2) stands in for the Kolhapur State of all years, including the eleven feudatory jagirs (Ichalkaranji, Kagal, Vishalgad, Bavda and others). Inside the Maratha Empire shape.

region.text: the Kolhapur State: about 8,200 km2 including jagirs

ledger.note: 1710: the Kolhapur branch of the Bhonsle family is established. "The states of Satara and Kolhapur came into being in 1707" over the succession; the infobox gives Kolhapur "established 1710"; Tarabai set up her rival court at Kolhapur in 1709 and her son was deposed by Rajasbai in 1714, who installed Sambhaji II. In 1731 Sambhaji II signed the Treaty of Warna with Shahu, formalising "two separate seats of Bhonsle family"; the page gives no boundary terms and no ground fought over, so no contest is drawn.

region.text: the Kolhapur State: about 8,200 km2 including jagirs

ledger.note: 1 March 1949: Kolhapur merges into Bombay State. Acceded to the Dominion of India on 14 August 1947; "merged into Bombay State" on 1 March 1949.

wars.name: Maratha succession war (Satara and Kolhapur)
wars.outcome: Shahu beat the regent at the Battle of Khed (undated) and the two branches settled by the Treaty of Warna in 1731, formalising "two separate seats of Bhonsle family"; Palkhed (1728) ended the Nizam's support for Sambhaji II.

wars.name: British expeditions against Kolhapur
wars.outcome: The British sent expeditions against Kolhapur in 1765 and 1792; the page gives no territorial result.

wars.name: Gadkari revolt of 1844
wars.outcome: A revolt against the British began in 1844 after the regent Daji Krishna Pandit was installed in 1843; Babaji Ahirekar was killed in December 1844.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary; the state is a circle about Kolhapur and its jagirs.

sources.title: Kolhapur State
sources.note: Founding 1707/1710, Warna 1731, 1765 and 1792 expeditions, 1901 area 8,332 km2, rulers, 14 August 1947, 1 March 1949.

sources.title: Tarabai
sources.note: Tarabai rival court at Kolhapur 1709; Shivaji deposed 1714; reconciled with Shahu 1730; died 9 December 1761.

sources.title: Sambhaji II of Kolhapur
sources.note: Reign 24 April 1813 to 2 July 1821; silent on the Treaty of Warna, territory, the Peshwa and Sawantwadi.

sources.title: Shahu of Kolhapur
sources.note: Adopted 17 March 1884; reign 2 April 1894 to 6 May 1922; reforms; Radhanagari Dam 1907-1935; silent on territory, the Political Agent and the Southern Maratha Country.

notes: Four pages opened (Kolhapur State, Tarabai, Sambhaji II of Kolhapur, Shahu of Kolhapur); the Treaty of Warna page returned url_not_found. The last two pages give reign dates only (Sambhaji 24 April 1813 to 2 July 1821; Shahu adopted 17 March 1884, reigned 2 April 1894 to 6 May 1922) and are silent on territory, Warna, the Peshwa, Sawantwadi, the Political Agent and the Southern Maratha Country. The pages give no territory before 1901 and say nothing of the Warna boundary, Sawantwadi, the Southern Maratha Country, Panhala as a seat, or the 1812 treaty (the page: "After 1818 Kolhapur entered treaty relations with the British"; the exact date of the 1812 treaty is not given). The state lies inside the maratha-empire shape until 1818 (the maratha-empire dossier already records a split of kolhapur-state in 1707). british-empire (sa-06) should record a vassal_start for kolhapur-state from the first treaty to 1947. Counterpart note: satara-state (restored 1818, annexed 1848) has a dossier in this batch. Founding year: 1707 (text), 1709 (Tarabai page), 1710 (infobox).
